page: Amazon Web Services r8i.96xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 384 vCPUs and 192 physical cores with two threads per core, utilizing the x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. The system is equipped with 3072.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. It includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions for accelerated mathematical operations.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth, with read-only cached memory bandwidth reaching 30,551.22 GB/sec and uncached large block reads at 1,125.32 GB/sec. The instance excels in parallel processing tasks, showing top-tier results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Passmark database operations. However, single-core performance is moderate, placing in the middle 50% for stress-ng single-core tests. Additionally, while prompt processing for large language models is strong, text generation speeds are limited, and the instance lacks local NVMe storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

Given its massive memory footprint and high-density compute capabilities, the r8i.96xlarge offers high qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound enterprise workloads that require substantial RAM without the overhead of multiple smaller instances. It is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, Redis deployments, heavy database operations, software compilation, and complex data-processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r8i.96xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor and an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. It delivers 384 vCPUs, 192 physical cores, and 3072.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 7 GHz. This instance is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise database operations, and heavy multi-threaded data processing workloads.
